sources.note: Gives each retrieval step of a search agent a dense reward built from two ground-truth-conditioned signals — how much the step raised the model's likelihood of the correct answer, and how necessary the step looks in hindsight — and fuses them asymmetrically so that a step which helps locally but is redundant globally is discounted.
sources.title: BiCAA: Bidirectional Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Agent

sources.note: Re-scores a search agent's own sampled tokens under a teacher that has been shown the instance's supporting evidence, and uses the detached teacher-student gap to nudge the GRPO advantage up or down on search and answer tokens only, without adding a distillation loss or changing anything at inference.
sources.title: EviSD: Evidence-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Search-Augmented Agents

sources.note: Estimates what a continuous latent thought is worth by freezing the context after it and averaging the rewards of several answers sampled from that fixed context, then credits latent positions with the resulting thought-level advantage and answer positions with the ordinary group-relative one.
sources.title: Latent Thought Credit: Multi-Answer Credit Assignment for Latent Reasoning

sources.note: Inserts a stage before RL in which the model extracts textual lessons from its own successful and failed rollouts, filters them by measured marginal utility on a held-out probe set, and distills the surviving pool into its own weights — so that GRPO starts from a policy that fails all-eight-samples less often.
sources.title: Self-Improving Large Language Models via Progressive Experience Evolution

sources.note: Treats a policy's per-problem failure probability as a random variable over the problem distribution and shows that REINFORCE, pass@K training and MaxRL each optimize a single moment of it, then proposes minimizing the first T moments jointly — which is exactly minimizing the expected truncated number of rollouts needed to reach a first success.
sources.title: Beyond the Mean: Multi-Moment Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning

sources.note: Replaces PPO's scalar mean-squared-error critic head with a categorical predictor over a discretized value support trained by cross-entropy against Gaussian-smoothed targets, decodes it back to a scalar for an unchanged GAE update, and shows the resulting critic is better calibrated and produces near-symmetric advantages where the MSE critic penalizes failures two-to-three times harder than it rewards successes.
sources.title: Start Classifying: Categorical Critics for LLM Reinforcement Learning

sources.note: Supervises audio reasoning with per-question rubrics generated from the raw waveform, and keeps the signal alive as the policy improves by regenerating the rubrics from the model's own rollouts each step and pruning any criterion that every rollout satisfies or none does.
sources.title: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics as Rewards for Audio Reasoning

sources.note: Scores each reasoning step of a translation by how much appending it raises a frozen reference model's teacher-forced likelihood of the gold translation, and adds that as a dense per-step reward on top of sequence-level quality — after first establishing that explicit reasoning helps long and hard inputs while drifting on terminology and style.
sources.title: PAMT: Process-Aligned Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Domain Machine Translation

sources.note: Shows that GRPO's per-completion uniformity is frequency-skewed once credit is aggregated by solution structure — a recurring correct form accumulates positive coefficient mass proportional to how often it is sampled — and rebalances it by a rarity exponent over a partition built from deterministic cue signatures rather than a judge model.
sources.title: When Correct Solutions Repeat: Rarity-Aware Credit Redistribution for GRPO

sources.note: A GRPO variant that teaches multimodal models to refuse when a referred object is absent, without losing localization accuracy on cases where it is present.
sources.title: Teaching MLLMs to Say No: Generalized Referring Expression Comprehension via Refusal Calibrated GRPO

sources.note: Trains a multimodal agent to orchestrate twelve video-analysis tools for anomaly detection with GRPO under a dual reward that combines exact-match rule checks with an LLM judge scoring logicality, relevance and completeness, and releases the benchmark it is evaluated on.
sources.title: VTO: Visual Tool Orchestration for Video Anomaly Detection

sources.note: Uses chain-of-thought about required capabilities as training-time supervision for a skill retriever -- distilled from a teacher in stage one and refined by retrieval-rewarded GRPO in stage two -- so that at inference the model encodes the bare query with no generation at all.
sources.title: SkillReason: Reasoning-Enhanced Agent Skill Retrieval for Implicit User Requests

sources.note: Addresses wasted rollouts in critic-free RL on prompts where every sampled rollout is already correct and the advantage estimate is therefore zero.
sources.title: Miner: Mining Intrinsic Mastery for Data-Efficient RL in Large Reasoning Models

aliases: string - other names the sources use for the same thing

result.definition: Estimating how much better a sampled action or trajectory was than the baseline it should be compared against -- the quantity that multiplies the policy gradient and therefore decides what training actually optimises. In this archive the dominant estimator is group-relative: sample several completions for one prompt and normalise each reward by the group's mean and standard deviation, which removes the value network entirely and is why most sources here use it. The sources document what that choice costs. It yields exactly zero advantage whenever every rollout in a group agrees, so prompts the model has already mastered waste their rollouts; and it treats completions as exchangeable, which becomes a frequency skew once credit is aggregated by solution structure, since a recurring correct form accumulates positive coefficient mass in proportion to how often it is sampled. Several sources therefore modify the advantage rather than the reward -- nudging it up or down from a detached teacher-student log-probability gap on selected token classes, replacing the group-relative advantage at latent positions with a thought-level value obtained by freezing the context and averaging over several sampled answers, or rebalancing it by a rarity exponent. Two sources argue about the target rather than the estimator: one shows that REINFORCE, pass@K training and MaxRL each optimise a single moment of the per-problem failure probability and proposes minimising the first several jointly, which is equivalent to minimising the expected truncated number of rollouts to a first success; the other keeps a learned critic but replaces its scalar mean-squared-error head with a categorical predictor over a discretised value support, reporting that the MSE critic had been penalising failures two to three times harder than it rewarded successes and that the categorical one produces near-symmetric advantages under an otherwise unchanged update.
